lines.li: [us] How are you finding it here?
[them,their:tribal] The fires burn differently here, but I am learning your ways.
[them,their:empire] Plainer than home, and nobody bows, which takes some getting used to.
[them] Strange still, but I'm getting used to it.
[us] Say so if anything's wrong, and we'll see to it.
[us] Give it a season and it grows on you.
[us] Is {GUARDIAN} working you hard?
[them,their:lowtech] Hard, but my family would say that is how a teacher should be.
[them] Hard enough, and I've learned more than I did all last year.
[us] {GUARDIAN} says you're quick, for what it's worth.
[them] Then I'll keep at it.
[us] You look like you're somewhere else today.
[them,their:tribal] I was thinking of the camp, and who is sitting in my place at the fire.
[them] I was thinking about home, about what they're all doing now.
[us] It's a long year, but it does pass.
[us] Sit with us at supper tonight, it helps to have company.
[them] I'm starting to know where everything is.
[us] Took me longer than that when I first came.
[us] Good, then you can stop asking me where the shovels are.
[us] You seem to have settled in.
[them,their:empire] Do not tell my family, but I may miss this place.
[them] I like it here more than I thought I would.
[us] Then we're doing something right.
[them] Does everyone here get up this early?
[us] Only the ones who want breakfast.
[us] Can't sleep?
[them,their:hightech] It's too quiet, there's always something humming at home.
[them] It's the quiet I'm not used to.
[us] You'll miss it when you're back in the noise.
[us] What do they have you doing today?
[them,their:empire] Carrying things, mostly, which at home would be a servant's work.
[them] Whatever needs doing, same as everyone.
[us] That's most days here.
[them] The food here isn't what I'm used to.
[us] Tell {COOK} what you miss, and it might turn up one night.
[them] I'll try, if I can describe it.
[them] Is it always like that, the fighting?
[us] Not always, but often enough that we keep the walls mended.
[them] I didn't know where to stand.
[us] Next time, inside and away from the doors.
[them] I'm sorry about {DEAD}, I didn't know them long.
[us] Thank you, that's kind.
[them] At court nobody would let me near a cookfire.
[us] Here nobody lets you near a meal unless you've been near the fire.
[them] I'm starting to see the sense in it.
[us] Do you miss your family?
[them] Sometimes, at night mostly.
[us] They'll be so proud of you when you go home.
[them] I learned something new today!
[us] Then you can show me after supper.
[them] How is {WARD} getting on with you?
[us] Well enough, and learning.
[them,their:lowtech] Tell {WARD} their family asks after them every evening.
[them] Tell {WARD} we ask after them.
[them] Who is teaching {WARD}?
[us] {GUARDIAN}, as patient as anyone here.
[them] Good, they'll need patience.
[them,their:tribal] {WARD} runs with our young hunters now and keeps up.
[them,their:medieval] {WARD} is up before the cooks and works until dark.
[them,their:hightech] {WARD} asks a lot of questions, which our teachers like.
[them] {WARD} is doing well with us.
[us] Good, we hoped they would fit in.
[them] Some of us will miss them when the year is out.
[them] Your page has learned to stand still through a whole audience.
[us] That's more than most of us could manage.
[them] The household is pleased with {WARD}, and says so to anyone at court.
[them] I spent a year here when I was young.
[us] Did you, and how does it look now?
[them] Smaller, and I mean that kindly.
[them] Different, but I still know my way around.
[us] Then welcome back.
[them] Part of whoever I am now, I learned at your colony.
[us] Then we're glad you came back to see it.
[them] People at home still talk about the year your colony kept one of our youths.
[us] We were glad to have them.
[them,their:lowtech] It is the kind of thing a house remembers for a long time.
[them] It's the kind of thing a family remembers.
[us] Do you have everything you need?
[them,their:lowtech] A bed and a place at your table, which is more than a hostage expects.
[them] More than I expected to have.
[us] You're one of us until the term is out.
[them] I count the days until the term is out.
[us] So do your people, I expect.
[us] Do you think the truce will hold?
[them] I hope so, with my own neck on it.
[us] Then we both hope so.
[them] Is {HOSTAGE} kept well?
[us] As well as anyone here, and you can ask them yourself.
[them] That's all we ask until the term is out.
[them,their:tribal] {HOSTAGE} sits with our elders in the evenings and listens.
[them,their:hightech] {HOSTAGE} has a room of their own and asks for nothing.
[them] {HOSTAGE} is well, and eats at our table.
[us] Tell them we haven't forgotten them.
[them] What will you do with {HOSTAGE}, now our people have broken their word?
[us] That's for the council to decide.
[them] Then I hope your council is kinder than our leaders were.
[us] Is {HOSTAGE} still alive?
[them] Alive, and held, as your colony knew they would be.
[us] Then we'll find a way to get them back.
[them] You sent our hostage home when the term was out, as you said you would.
[us] That was the agreement.
[them,their:lowtech] Not every people keeps to its word, so it was noticed.
[them] Not everyone keeps to an agreement, so it was noticed.
